chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from his father, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites the Surahs of Al-Ankabut and Ar-Rum during the month of Ramadan on the night of the twenty-third, he is, by Allah, O Abu Muhammad, among the people of Paradise. I do not exclude him ever, nor do I fear that Allah will write upon me in my right [hand/book of deeds] a sin, and indeed these two Surahs have a high status with Allah.

key_terms.الرُّومِ: Ar-Rum (The Romans), the 30th chapter of the Quran
key_terms.سُورَهَ الْعَنْکَبُوتِ: Surah Al-Ankabut (The Spider), the 29th chapter of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ankabut and Ar-Rum on the 23rd night of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq emphasizes the specific merit of reciting Surah Al-Ankabut and Surah Ar-Rum together on Laylat al-Qadr (the 23rd night), linking the themes of divine testing and the victory of the believers to the spiritual elevation of Ramadan. The Imam’s absolute assurance of Paradise ('min ahl al-jannah') underscores the high status of these Surahs in Shia devotional practice, particularly for their focus on the signs of God in history and the natural world.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from his father from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “O Aba Muhammad!

One who recites Surah Ankaboot and Room on the twenty-third of the month of Ramadan would be included among the people of Paradise. I do not expect anything. Allah would not write any sins of this type. These two Surahs have a high regard near Allah.”
